headline: SpaceX soars. Avanti shrinks. AI bets intensify.
deck: SpaceX's IPO boosts confidence while Avanti's sale signals caution in the satellite market.

stories.head: SpaceX shares jump nearly 20% in IPO
stories.body: SpaceX's shares surged by almost 20% following its IPO, valuing the company at an eye-watering $470 billion. This leap suggests that even in the realm of space, investor enthusiasm can reach stratospheric heights. The performance underscores the public's appetite for space ventures, despite the usual skepticism around profitability.
stories.soWhat: If SpaceX can pull this off, expect other space ventures to follow suit, hoping to hitch a ride on the hype train.

stories.head: Avanti sells Hylas-3, reducing GEO footprint
stories.body: Avanti Communications is offloading its Hylas-3 satellite to streamline its operations and reduce exposure in the geostationary orbit market. This move hints at a strategic pivot as the company grapples with the realities of a saturated satellite landscape. The sale reflects a growing consensus that less can indeed be more in this sector.
stories.soWhat: Avanti's retreat from GEO could signal a broader trend of consolidation as companies reassess their market positions.

stories.head: Astra doubles down on AI amid uncertainty
stories.body: Astra's CEO Chris Kemp is betting the company's future on AI technologies, a decision that raises eyebrows given the company's rocky launch history. With competitors ramping up their own AI initiatives, Astra's pivot may be a last-ditch effort to stay relevant in an increasingly crowded field. The emphasis on AI could either be a masterstroke or a sign of desperation.
stories.soWhat: If Astra's AI gamble pays off, it might just redefine how we think about launch operations; if not, it could lead to a swift exit from the market.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension implications
watchlist.body: With Palantir securing a $480 million extension, watch for increased focus on government contracts as a stable revenue stream.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser progress
watchlist.body: After passing its critical design review, the real test for Sierra Space will be turning plans into a functioning spacecraft.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic test delays continue
watchlist.body: The ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing could impact defense timelines and funding allocations.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's Series C impact
watchlist.body: True Anomaly's $190 million raise might signal a shift in co-orbital security priorities, especially with DoD backing.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
